title: Flu-like illness falls to 7.2% of clinic visits in Pontotoc’s health district
excerpt: For the week ending Nov. 14, the northeast district’s share of visits for flu-like symptoms fell from 7.9% to 7.2%. Mississippi’s statewide share rose to 4.1%.
locality: MSDH District II in Northeast Mississippi includes Pontotoc County. Counts of patients seen in the story refer to Mississippi statewide.

paragraphs.text: Flu-like symptoms accounted for 7.2% of visits to participating clinics in the Northeast Mississippi health district that includes Pontotoc County during the week ending Nov. 14. That share fell from 7.9% the week before, even as the statewide share rose from 3.5% to 4.1%, according to the Mississippi State Department of Health.

The northeast recorded the second-highest share among Mississippi’s nine districts. Only District III, in the Delta, reported a higher figure, at 15.1%. The state publishes one figure for the northeast district, which also includes Lee, Union and eight other counties. The report gives no separate rate for Pontotoc County.

Across Mississippi, participating providers reported 721 patients with flu-like symptoms among 17,446 seen Nov. 8–14. A week earlier they reported 607 among 17,322. The reporting network varies from week to week. The department received 62 provider reports for the latest week and 60 for the previous one.

Clinics count a patient in this measure when they record a fever of at least 100 degrees Fahrenheit along with a cough or sore throat. A positive flu test is not required. The department tracks those visits to see how illness changes over time and may revise the figures as more providers report.
